subject: Private deployment: BYOK, operator access, and escrow expectations
messages:
From: Anna Morozov <anna@skybridgehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skybridgehealth.com
Date: 2028-10-29T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment terms - operator access & BYOK

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we discussed on the call, Skybridge Health is evaluating Redwood's private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for a regulated workload. Before we proceed to procurement, legal and engineering asked for a short written summary covering three items:

1) BYOK and key custody — who creates and holds the CMKs, escrow conditions, and whether Redwood retains any copy of customer keys.
2) Operator access and telemetry — what operational roles (if any) Redwood engineers have against the private runtime and what telemetry/logs you collect.
3) Cross-border transfers and subprocessors — especially where key material or operational support may be located.

Can you please provide a baseline position and a short mutual action plan (MAP) with required evidence (SOC2 excerpts, keystore diagrams, escrow policy) and expected turnaround? We'd like to get to a negotiated annex rather than a long back-and-forth.

If it helps, we can do a 30-min alignment call next week.

Thanks,
Anna Morozov
Lead Counsel, Skybridge Health
anna@skybridgehealth.com

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment terms - operator access & BYOK

Anna —

Appreciate the clear ask. High level position below and a proposed MAP attached (attachment: redwood_privdep_byok_annex_v1.pdf).

BYOK / keystore:
- Customers generate and control the customer master key (CMK) in their KMS (cloud KMS or on-prem HSM).
- For VPC and on-prem installs we do not retain customer key material; Redwood runs against encrypted model artifacts and only receives ciphertext.
- Escrow: we offer an optional keystore-escrow addendum — escrow release requires a joint trigger (customer request + legal confirmation for account termination or catastrophe). Escrow is an audited HSM custody held with a third-party escrow provider; we can provide the escrow policy and SLA.

Operator access / telemetry:
- Default operator role is "ops-assist": limited to orchestration and health checks. No direct access to keystore plaintext or model KV cache.
- Telemetry is configurable: by default we collect aggregated CPU/GPU utilization, request latencies, and token counts; sampling of debug traces is off unless enabled via a Support request and documented in the MAP.
- Breakglass: a documented, auditable breakglass process exists for emergencies — timeboxed access, logged to an immutable audit sink, and requires two internal approvals (SRE + Security).

Subprocessors & transfers:
- Operational personnel supporting the private deployment may be located in EU and US; any cross-border support is described in our subprocessor roster and we can restrict support regions per contract.
- We will commit to no customer key exfiltration and no caching of plaintext PII in logs.

Attached is a draft annex and a proposed MAP with evidence items and timelines. Can we do a 30-minute call on Tue 11/07 or Wed 11/08?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
(attachment: redwood_privdep_byok_annex_v1.pdf)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment terms - operator access & BYOK

Anna / Laura —

Adding a few technical clarifications that customers frequently request so legal can align the annex language with operational reality:

- Keystore architecture: Customer CMK is only referenced by the runtime; Redwood's process images never instantiate the CMK in our tenancy. For cloud KMS BYOK we use the KMS-as-a-service interface; for on-prem HSM we support PKCS#11 or cloud-HSM gateway.

- KV cache / model context: KV cache (LLM attention/state) is in-memory only on the inference nodes and is never written to persistent disk. We can add contractual language that nodes use encrypted swap only and that swap does not contain plaintext request data.

- Telemetry detail: we can offer an "aggregated-only" telemetry profile that redacts per-request text and only surface bucketed latency/token bins + health counters. If Skybridge requires zero-per-request telemetry, we can move to a self-hosted telemetry collector for your team to manage.

- Escrow triggers: Typical triggers we see are (a) provider insolvency, (b) contractual termination without data retrieval, (c) regulatory hold. We are open to refining the list and adding a mediation step prior to release.

Happy to walk through diagrams on the call — I can share a short architecture sketch live.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Thanks Laura and Kim — this is helpful. A few items from legal + procurement that we'd like to capture in the annex and MAP before we move to signature: 

1) Escrow: we prefer escrow release to require (i) customer-signed release + (ii) independent escrow custodian attestation. Can Redwood confirm whether the escrow provider supports attestation and can provide sample SLA wording?

2) Operator role definition: please include explicit forbidden activities (e.g., "no access to KV cache, no rekeying of CMKs, no extraction of request payloads into logs"). We also need the breakglass time/window and an SLA for post-incident audit evidence delivery (paper trail within 72 hours).

3) Subprocessors: please share the minimal subprocessor list we need to include in our DPA with region tags. We will propose that any non-EU support be treated as opt-in and require prior notice.

Procurement also asked for: SOC2 excerpt showing key custody controls (see attached), and a copy of the proposed annex redlines by 11/06 so we can put the MAP on our internal procurement calendar.

Anna
Anna Morozov
Lead Counsel, Skybridge Health

Anna —

Thanks for the precision; appreciate the SOC excerpt. Quick summary from our side and suggested next steps so procurement has dates to work with: 

- Escrow: Redwood confirms escrow custodian attestation is available; we will provide the escrow SLA and sample attestation template in the MAP (deliverable by 11/08). Escrow release will require customer instruction + custodian attestation; Redwood legal proposes adding a 7-day mediation hold for non-emergency requests.

- Forbidden operator activities: we will add explicit forbidden-activity bullets to the annex: no KV-cache dumps, no CMK materialization by Redwood staff, no plaintext request logging. Breakglass access is time-limited (max 48 hours) and audited; post-incident package (audit logs, access timeline, justification) delivered within 72 hours.

- Subprocessors: attached to this thread is a minimal initial subprocessor roster (included in the MAP). For Skybridge we can contractually restrict support regions to EU-only unless you opt-in to US-based support.

Next steps / MAP milestones: 
1) Redwood to deliver updated annex + escrow SLA + subprocessor roster by 2028-11-08.
2) Skybridge to deliver redlines and procurement gating items by 2028-11-15.
3) Joint call to review redlines w/ Kim (security) on 2028-11-16 — we can host at 09:00 GMT.

DocuSign link for the base SOW/PO will be provided once the annex is agreed; in the meantime I have added the HubSpot deal and the MAP to our internal tracker.

Regards,
